Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps I promised: 

Recap:
- FinPay workload: conversational customer support + realtime personalization calls.
- Current baseline: ~100 requests/sec steady; expected burst up to ~800 req/sec during peak campaign windows.
- Latency objective: p95 end-to-end inference < 200ms for short prompts (under ~256 tokens); p50 target < 120ms.
- Key constraint: single-region hosting in us-west, PCI/PII concerns managed through encryption, but FinPay prefers provider-managed isolation for peak workloads.

What we discussed re: deployment modes:
- Hosted API: simplest to run; scales automatically and is low-friction, but cold-starts and multi-tenant contention can occasionally push p95 beyond 200ms at very high concurrency without a reserved plan.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools give predictable throughput and lower variance on p95; recommended if you need strict latency SLOs during sustained peak windows.
- Private VPC/on-prem: best for strict data residency/compliance; higher ops overhead.

Next steps I will take:
1) Send a short benchmark request form so we can capture sample payloads and traffic patterns (attached).
2) Share our recent Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark PDF and a short summary of expected throughput-per-GPU for the models we discussed.
3) Offer a two-week Dedicated pilot (isolated pool) so you can run your traffic and validate p95/p50 under production-like conditions.

Could you fill out the attached form (or paste a representative sample request) and confirm whether you want us to provision a pilot pool next week?

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 30-min tech session with Marissa if you want to run through the benchmarks live.

Best,

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the questions — summary below and attached is our benchmark PDF (redwood_dedicated_benchmarks_20270320.pdf) that includes raw test plots and test configuration so your infra team can validate. Key points up front:

Hosted API (typical, multi-tenant) — model: redwood-13b-moderate (same family we discussed)
- 100 req/sec steady: p50 ~ 60–90ms; p95 ~ 140–190ms (varies with prompt length & total tokens).
- 800 req/sec burst: p50 ~ 120–180ms; p95 can rise to 300–450ms during large concurrent bursts without reserved capacity.
- Note: Hosted handles autoscaling but prioritizes cluster utilization; for strict p95 SLOs we typically recommend a reserved plan (Dedicated) or a burst commitment.

Dedicated capacity (per-GPU throughput example — n1-standard serving config):
- Single GPU (A100-class) serving redwood-13b-moderate: sustained throughput ~200–300 req/sec for short prompts (<=256 tokens) with p50 ~ 40–70ms and p95 ~ 80–130ms under controlled load.
- 4-GPU pool (common minimal Dedicated reserve): aggregate sustained ~800–1200 req/sec; p95s observed in our tests ~90–160ms depending on batching and key-value cache hit rates.
- Dedicated pools are isolated and give consistent jitter reduction; autoscaling can be configured (policy-based) to add nodes, and we can enable a short-duration burst capacity that spins up extra instances (subject to region capacity). Typical spin-up for extra nodes is minutes (we can pre-warm if you want immediate burst headroom).

Pilot offer:
- We can provision a 2-week Dedicated pilot in us-west with a 4-GPU pool pre-warmed for your traffic. You'll be able to run your production traffic through the pool (we'll provide traffic-safeguarded hooks) and we'll collect p50/p95 metrics and KV cache effectiveness.
- If the pilot validates the p95 < 200ms requirement during your peak scenarios, next step is a reserved commit conversation for predictable capacity and pricing.

Attachments in this thread: redwood_dedicated_benchmarks_20270320.pdf (benchmarks + test configs), finpay_benchmark_request_form.pdf (filled sample helps accelerate pilot setup).

Shall I go ahead and provision the pilot for Monday? If yes, I'll loop in Marissa (solutions eng) to schedule the onboarding & test plan.
